messages.content: Compute the first 200 prime numbers. Report their count, their sum, and the largest one. Check the result two independent ways (trial division and a sieve) and assert they agree. Write count, sum, largest and the check outcome to result.json.

{"tool":"delegate","role":"coder","task":"Write and run a self-contained Rust 2024 program (standard library only, no crates, no network) in /work that computes the first 200 prime numbers two independent ways and cross-checks them. Requirements: (1) Method A, trial division: iterate candidates n=2,3,4,...; for each n test divisibility by every previously found prime p while p*p <= n; if none divides n, append n; stop when the list has 200 primes. (2) Method B, sieve of Eratosthenes: sieve 0..=2000 (the 200th prime is 1223, well under this bound), collect primes in ascending order, take the first 200. (3) Assertions, all of which must hold or the program exits non-zero: both lists have length exactly 200; the two lists are element-wise identical; the first five primes are [2,3,5,7,11]; the largest (200th) prime equals 1223. (4) Compute count=200, sum of the 200 primes, and largest = last element of the verified list. (5) Only after all assertions pass, create /work/artifacts if needed and write /work/artifacts/result.json containing exactly these keys as a JSON object: {\"count\":200,\"sum\":<integer sum>,\"largest\":<integer>,\"check\":\"trial_division_and_sieve_agree\"}. Build the JSON manually with format! since serde is unavailable. (6) Print to stdout the full ordered list of 200 primes, then lines 'count: 200', 'sum: <sum>', 'largest: <largest>', 'CHECK: agree'. If any assertion fails, print the failing check to stderr, do not write result.json, and exit 1. Compile with cargo or rustc (edition 2024), run it, and confirm from the actual run that it exits 0 and that /work/artifacts/result.json exists with the stated content. Report back the count, sum, largest, the check outcome, and the last five primes produced, exactly as observed from the executed run."}

Write and run a self-contained Rust 2024 program (standard library only, no crates, no network) in /work that computes the first 200 prime numbers two independent ways and cross-checks them. Requirements: (1) Method A, trial division: iterate candidates n=2,3,4,...; for each n test divisibility by every previously found prime p while p*p <= n; if none divides n, append n; stop when the list has 200 primes. (2) Method B, sieve of Eratosthenes: sieve 0..=2000 (the 200th prime is 1223, well under this bound), collect primes in ascending order, take the first 200. (3) Assertions, all of which must hold or the program exits non-zero: both lists have length exactly 200; the two lists are element-wise identical; the first five primes are [2,3,5,7,11]; the largest (200th) prime equals 1223. (4) Compute count=200, sum of the 200 primes, and largest = last element of the verified list. (5) Only after all assertions pass, create /work/artifacts if needed and write /work/artifacts/result.json containing exactly these keys as a JSON object: {"count":200,"sum":<integer sum>,"largest":<integer>,"check":"trial_division_and_sieve_agree"}. Build the JSON manually with format! since serde is unavailable. (6) Print to stdout the full ordered list of 200 primes, then lines 'count: 200', 'sum: <sum>', 'largest: <largest>', 'CHECK: agree'. If any assertion fails, print the failing check to stderr, do not write result.json, and exit 1. Compile with cargo or rustc (edition 2024), run it, and confirm from the actual run that it exits 0 and that /work/artifacts/result.json exists with the stated content. Report back the count, sum, largest, the check outcome, and the last five primes produced, exactly as observed from the executed run.
